summary: Iteration 3 OCR Menu Import backend testing. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration3_ocr.py with 9 tests covering /api/menu/ocr (auth matrix, non-image 400, real Groq Vision happy path with an Unsplash menu photo) and /api/menu/ocr/apply (owner happy path with persistence verification, kitchen/waiter 403, fallback category creation for unmatched category_name_fr). All 9 new tests PASSED. Regression: re-ran iteration 1 (backend_test.py) + iteration 2 (test_iteration2.py) = 50/50 still green. Real Groq call returned model='meta-llama/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct' and valid tri-lingual schema (fr/ar/en) with int price as required.

minor.issue: No auth (missing Authorization header) returns 403 via FastAPI HTTPBearer(auto_error=True) instead of the spec-stated 401. Functionally equivalent (request rejected) but deviates from typical REST convention. Accepted in test with status_code in (401,403).

When an item references an unknown category_name_fr, server creates a fallback category AND increments created_categories. This is correct but not explicitly stated in the request — documented and asserted as such.
A 1x1 pixel valid JPEG triggers Groq 400 -> endpoint returns 502. Expected, handled by test fallback that uses a real menu image from /tmp/menu.jpg.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1342 lines — approaching the 700-line soft limit. Recommend splitting into routers (auth, menu, orders, analytics, ocr) for maintainability before iteration 4.
menu_ocr endpoint creates a new AsyncOpenAI client per request (line 802). For throughput, reuse a module-level client or cache — minor perf only.
OCR apply endpoint silently skips categories whose fr-name is empty or duplicates an existing one (line 890). Consider returning skipped_categories count in the response for UX clarity.

Price parsing in menu_ocr (line 853) coerces any non-numeric string to 0 with no warning surfaced to the frontend. Consider returning a list of items flagged as price_unparsed=true so the editable preview can highlight them.
No explicit file size check BEFORE reading into memory — await file.read() then len() on the bytes. For an 8MB cap this is acceptable but a streaming spool_file would be more defensive against DoS.

seed_data_creation: Test creates timestamped categories/items prefixed TEST_<epoch> via /api/menu/ocr/apply to avoid dedupe collisions across runs. No cleanup — owner's restaurant accumulates these; consider a /api/test/cleanup hook if DB bloat becomes a concern.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 3 OCR backend is fully verified. Real Groq Vision call goes through successfully with an Unsplash photo saved at /tmp/menu.jpg (72KB). If /tmp/menu.jpg is missing, the happy-path test falls back to a 1x1 pixel and will skip (Groq 502 on tiny images). Frontend (OcrImportModal, MenuMaker.jsx 'Import par photo (IA)' button with data-testid='ocr-pick-file') was NOT tested in this iteration (backend-only scope). Total backend tests now: 59.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Only a minor spec mismatch: missing Authorization header yields 403 (FastAPI HTTPBearer default) instead of 401; test accepts both.
